name: Cummins India Ltd.
business_summary: Indian arm of Cummins Inc. (USA, 51% promoter). Designs, makes and services diesel and alternative-fuel engines (2.8-100 L) and generator sets up to 3 MW, plus alternators, filtration, turbo components and aftermarket. Segments: Power Generation (largest, includes data-centre and commercial backup), Industrial (rail, mining, construction, marine, defence), Distribution (parts and service) and exports. Debt-free, ~70% payout, high ROE (30%). FY26 sales Rs 12,143 cr, OPM 21%; the Sep-2026 quarter shows OPM collapsing to 15%, the key debate. Revenue-segment splits are from model knowledge, not freshly sourced.

exposures.mechanism: Copper (alternator windings, cables, imported Stamford alternators) ~8% of costs (model estimate; materials+resale were 66.5% of revenue in Q1 FY27 vs 63.0%). +10% copper -> costs +0.8% -> at 15% OPM EBITDA -5.3%; ~50% passed on with a 1-2 quarter lag -> -2.7%; EV/MCap ~0.97; persistence 0.25 -> ~-0.65, rounded to -0.8 given Q2 evidence that recovery is lagging. Pack shows +0.89 (t=+1.1) which is demand-cycle co-movement, not a cost channel; disagreement noted, weight shrunk toward zero range.
Steel/castings/forgings ~12% of costs (model estimate). +7% -> costs +0.84% -> EBITDA -5.6% at 15% OPM; half recovered via price lists with a lag; persistence 0.3; EV/MCap 0.97 -> ~-0.8.
Aluminium (alternator/engine castings) ~4% of costs; +10% -> costs +0.4% -> EBITDA -2.7%; half recovered, persistence 0.25 -> ~-0.3.

Domestic power-gen is ~45% of revenue (model estimate). +5 pp realised-price erosion on that slice = -2.25% of revenue, nearly all falling to EBITDA -> EBITDA -15% at 15% OPM; persistence 0.5; EV/MCap 0.97 -> ~-7. Q2 FY27 OPM fell ~680 bp YoY (22%->15%) and revenue grew only 4%, consistent with price/mix/cost-recovery pressure; cause not confirmed from management commentary (earnings call not retrieved).

evidence.source: pack: screener.in + Google News headlines (ET, NDTV Profit, CNBC TV18)
evidence.note: Q2 FY27 OPM 15% vs 22% a year ago; stock -10 to -15% on result day

exposures.mechanism: Industrial engines, gensets and distribution are capex-linked. +10% private capex growth -> revenue elasticity ~0.6 -> +6% revenue; incremental EBITDA margin ~30% of revenue -> EBITDA +1.8% of revenue = +12% on 15% OPM; persistence 0.5; EV/MCap 0.97 -> ~+5.8, haircut to +5 for operating-leverage uncertainty.

Infrastructure, mining, rail, construction-equipment engines and large gensets for public projects. +10% govt capex -> revenue +2.5% -> EBITDA +5% (30% incremental margin on 15% OPM) -> x0.5 persistence x0.97 -> ~+2.5.

Data-centre backup power is a headline growth driver (HDFC Sky 2026-10-01 'capex revival' piece; a Q2 FY26 analyst note flagged data-centre execution as unusually high and not repeating at that scale). Assume DC ~15% of power-gen orders; +1 theme unit = +20% DC demand -> +3% revenue at 35% contribution margin -> EBITDA +7%; persistence 0.6 -> ~+4. Wide range because DC order lumpiness and price competition erode the margin.

Exports ~20-25% of revenue (model estimate) vs imported components (alternators, electronics, group purchases) ~16% of revenue. +3% USD/INR: export revenue +0.7% of revenue, imported cost +0.5% of revenue -> net ~+0.2% of revenue, largely hedged -> ~neutral.

Debt-free (interest Rs 3 cr/qtr) so no funding cost; effect is via valuation duration (P/E 49.5, ROE 30%) and customers' financing of capex. +25 bp -> ~-1% on a long-duration multiple, in line with high-P/E capital goods.

Pack: +2.53 per +5% S&P (t=+3.1, beta to Nifty 0.73). Interpreted as AI/data-centre capex and parent-group (Cummins Inc.) sentiment proxy; mechanism partly overlaps T_DATA_CENTRES_IN so central weight shrunk slightly.

Pack shows -3.78 per +15% coal (t=-2.3) but there is no clear fundamental channel (coal-fired power buyers are not genset customers; higher coal = India power cost stress could even raise backup-power demand). Weight shrunk to -1.0 pending a mechanism; treat as statistical.

Exports (Middle East, Africa, Europe, SE Asia) are ~20-25% of revenue; GCC infrastructure/oil-gas capex drives export gensets and engines. +1 pp GCC growth -> export revenue +1.5% -> EBITDA +3% -> x0.5 -> ~+1.
Small direct US export share; indirect via Cummins group intercompany flows and Indian customers' capex confidence. +10 pp tariff -> ~-0.7.

supply_chain.note: 51% promoter; technology licences, royalties, imported components and export channel. US EPA heavy-duty NOx rules weigh on parent sentiment (UBS target cut 2026-09-30, Investing.com).

supply_chain.counterparty: Kirloskar Oil Engines, Caterpillar/Rolls-Royce mtu, Mahindra Powerol, Kohler
supply_chain.note: Genset price competition; none of the listed peers in Nifty 200 data set

current_state.latest_quarter: Q2 FY27 (Sep 2026): sales Rs 3,301 cr per screener (+4% YoY; press cites Rs 3,247 cr), OPM 15% vs 22%, net profit Rs 507 cr (-18% YoY; one outlet cites Rs 467 cr after exceptional items). Q1 FY27: OPM 18%.
current_state.trend: Three consecutive quarters of falling OPM (21% -> 18% -> 15%) with flat-to-low growth; stock -15% on result day, -23% over 3 months.
current_state.valuation: P/E 49.5, P/B 14, market cap Rs 1.15 lakh cr (screener, 2026-11-05) before part of the result-day fall; 5y profit CAGR 31%. Historically a premium-multiple stock; de-rating risk if OPM does not recover.

key_risks: Margin reset: price competition in gensets and slow cost pass-through; cause not yet confirmed from the earnings call
Data-centre order lumpiness and price pressure
Valuation (P/E ~50) leaves little room for further misses
Parent-group (Cummins Inc.) regulatory/sentiment overhang from EPA rules
upside_triggers: Evidence that Q2 margin hit is one-off (mix, provisions, warranty, inventory) and Q3 OPM returns to 18%+
Cost deflation in copper/aluminium (aluminium -19.6% since June)
